decided_by: Claude (Fable QA fix round A-03; David 2026-10-25 "do all fixes")
basis: Fable QA A-03 (and A-02): GTAP 12 ch.17A p.2 item 4 holds the tax rates for purchases of domestic and imported goods across all agents (item 5 the export and output tax rates); the tax money then moves with the fitted flows. The round-3 rule (general_part_money_held_by_column_rates_rescaled_after_each_fit_pass, round-3 final QA item 3) held the general part of every column's product tax in money and rescaled its rates by 0.5 to 2.0, with 1,609 columns at the 2x bound, which is the opposite constraint and was tagged gtap without a page. GTAP's revenue control is in the prior, not in the FIT: ch.8 Appendix A scales the expected tax revenue on the I-O flows to the revenue government reports; here that is the io_s12 TLS (ICIO, national tables), the G114 money of the representative-table regions (product_tax_source), the GCC VAT (vat_final_demand) and the energy taxes at their S10 revenue (energy_tax_revenue), all set on the prior flows. The fit then holds every cell's rate, so product-tax revenue moves with the fitted purchases (the round-3 QA saw about +172 bn worldwide, mostly in the EU, with GDP held and value added moving the other way). S13-Rptaxprior reports each region's fitted revenue against its prior. The money hold stays available as general_part_money_held_by_column_rates_rescaled_after_each_fit_pass.

Round-3 final QA item 4 (S11 worker's finding): the B15 fuel subsidy on a good S13 does not hold to an S11 target (electricity) was booked exactly in the prior (rho = S / (B0 + S)) and the fit then moved it with the purchases, so a region could book far more than S11 gives (IRN electricity well above its S11 amount), pushing factor income above GDP. GTAP books fuel subsidies as source money totals: Chepeliev, McDougall and van der Mensbrugghe (2018) §3.1-3.2, used by GTAP 12 ch.3 §3.2.4, subtract the subsidy from the commodity tax revenue so that the subsidy money equals the source estimate. method.hold_product_taxes: after each fit pass rho is reset on the fitted purchases, rho = S / (A + S) with A the purchases at the cell powers without the subsidy (purchasers' values kept), and the fit is solved again (warm start) until the fitted table books exactly S (1e-9); the other taxes in the cell keep their amount as in the B15 booking. The S11 electricity price is not used by S13, so this hold is the mechanism. Hard check S13-Hsubsidy now requires the fitted electricity subsidy to equal the S11 amount (less the NEERS subsidy on the row); S13-Hfacgdp checks factor income less GDP is at most the booked product subsidies in every region. prior_rate_moves_with_the_fit is the rule before this round.

Round-3 final QA2 item 1: product_tax_totals held each column at its io_s12 money, and for a region whose I-O table comes from S05 donors that money is the donor table pattern scaled to the region, so a region without a VAT carried its donor VAT (KWT household general rate about 0.33 on several goods from CYP; BHR, OMN, TTO, IRQ, LBY similar). GTAP 12 ch.9D uses the representative table for the structure of production, intermediate usage and consumption, not for the tax wedges; ch.8 Appendix A (Angola) puts tax rates on the I-O flows and scales the expected revenue to the actual revenue reported by government, and ch.15 takes government revenue from the IMF GFS. s13_fit/ptax_source.py: for every S05 donor region (donor_weights), the general (non-energy-excise) part of the product-tax rates is scaled by one factor so that its money on the io_s12 flows equals IMF GFS G114 taxes on goods and services (2022, percent of GDP, general government S13 where reported, else the central-government series; source data/imf_world, the IMF WoRLD compilation of GFS revenue) times S02 GDP, less the positive energy excise S13 books separately (fix list A1); the cell pattern is kept and product_tax_totals then holds that money through the fit. A composite takes the GDP-weighted G114 share of its members when the members with a value cover at least 90 percent of their GDP (our rule). A region without such a 2022 value (KWT, QAT, LBY, YEM, SYR, PAL, VEN, PRK and composites below the cover) has its rates held (no money hold), flagged PTAX-RATES-HELD. Hard check S13-Hptaxsource; S13-Rnovat reports the household general rate in KWT, QAT, IRQ and LBY (no VAT or general sales tax in 2022) against 2 percent. io_s12_money_every_region is the rule before.

The PSE electricity remainder is now netted against the whole IEA electricity amount, at most the smaller of the two (method.book_pse_input; netted_musd in pse_input_items_s13.csv); the IEA subsidy stays as booked, since it is held through the fit. Round 3 final QA 2 item 2: the IEA consumption subsidy was booked on every buyer, the energy industries' own purchases of energy included, so a subsidised diagonal (own use) inflated at basic prices. The IEA price-gap estimate covers fuels consumed by end users and electricity consumption; fuels used by the energy sector itself (own use, transformation in power plants and refineries) are not end use (Chepeliev, McDougall and van der Mensbrugghe 2018 §3, GTAP 12 ch.12 own use as a volume). The subsidy rate is set on final consumption and non-energy users only (method.subsidy_columns, the coa, oil, gas, pet and ely columns left out); the money stays the S11 IEA amount per region and good, now on the other buyers, held through the fit by the rate reset after each pass (as electricity_subsidy_money). A good that only energy activities buy keeps the old base (reported in the basis). Values-free basis. SET TO every_firm_household_government FOR THIS RUN (2026-10-25): with the exclusion the money-held rate reset on every good slowed the fit many times and one region diverged; the exclusion code stays (value final_consumption_and_non_energy_users_energy_industry_own_use_and_transformation_excluded_money_held) for a later pass with a bounded rate reset.

Round 3 final QA 2 item 2: the own-use cap (own_use_cap) was measured on purchasers' values, so a subsidised diagonal sat below the UNSD share while its basic value was a large share of output. GTAP 12 ch.12 places own use as a volume of the energy balance, valued at basic prices; the cap is now on the diagonal's basic value over the column (output) in the prior cap and in the second-pass overshoot test, and own_use_s13.csv reports the fitted diagonal at basic value (fitted_own_basic_musd, fitted_share_basic).
